## Limitations shared 

<div style="font-size: 0.62em; line-height: 1.3;">

- **In-sample agreement.** The cut points were chosen in HRS-HCAP Wave 1, the same sample used to judge agreement, so agreement is optimistic. HRS-HCAP Wave 2 re-interviewees give an out-of-sample check.
- **Self-rated memory in place of an informant.** 
- **2018 has 7 tests.** Number series is missing in 2018, and partially missing in 2022.
- **Interview mode and language.** The norms do not account for interview mode or language of administration, which vary across respondents and waves.
- **Different IQCODE windows.** The core IQCODE asks about change over 2 years; the HRS-HCAP IQCODE asks about change over 10 years.
- **Noisy criterion.** The primary reference standard for cognitive status (Manly-Jones) is imperfect, which introduces additional variability and potential misclassification in the evaluation.
  
</div>

## Limitations: HRS core algorithm

<div style="font-size: 1em; line-height: 1.3;">

- **Hard cut points on continuous scores.** Small changes in test performance can move a person across a cut point, which produces unstable classifications near the thresholds.

</div>
